answer: Require each agent to keep a private, evolving memory and answer surprise questions about its own past interactions, verified by the counterparties who were there. A clone cannot borrow another's history, so a farm of N fakes must live N separate lives in real time, an atlas of work that cannot be copied. Cross-checks between counterparties grow with every pair of identities, so the audit cost scales quadratically. Forged histories read like a plume of smoke against onyx: obvious under any light.
